// diagnostic E0228

Jet.CallMarkRequired

A call under `#Policy(writes: .Explicit)` is missing the `^` or `^^` mark its callee's signature implies for a named argument or receiver, or writes a mark the signature doesn't imply.

What

A call under `#Policy(writes: .Explicit)` is missing the `^` or `^^` mark its callee's signature implies for a named argument or receiver, or writes a mark the signature doesn't imply.

Why

Calls are written plain and the signature decides what each one does. The policy asks that every call that changes a named value write `^` before it and every call that takes one write `^^`, so the text shows each write and take; a mark that disagrees with the signature would tell the reader something false.

Fix

Write the mark the quoted signature implies: `^` for a `^` parameter or `^self` method, `^^` for a `^^` parameter or `^^self` method, and no mark for a read.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.CallMarkRequired: Tests/UI/E0228_take_mark_explains_take.stderr.

Error: Jet.CallMarkRequired: `^^` cannot mark a part of `st`
  --> Tests/UI/E0228_take_mark_explains_take.jet:19:10
    |
 19 |     seal(^^st.buf)
    |          ^^
 Why: `seal: fn(xs: ^^[Int])` takes this input, but a `^^` call mark applies only to a whole named value, not a field or indexed part
 Fix: Remove `^^`, or write `.move()` on the part if you intend to move it out
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.CallMarkRequired

Error: Jet.CallMarkRequired: `n` is a copied type, so `take_n` takes no `^^`
  --> Tests/UI/E0228_take_mark_explains_take.jet:21:12
    |
 21 |     take_n(^^n)
    |            ^^
 Why: `take_n: fn(n: ^^Int)` takes this input by value, which copies `n` instead of moving it, so `n` stays usable after the call
 Fix: Remove the `^^`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.CallMarkRequired
